reasons: Classification is correct: 14.2 grants Vendor exclusive ownership of Customer-commissioned Deliverables with only a revocable, non-transferable, Order-Form-term licence back, which fails the fallback's requirement of a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables — squarely within the detection guidance ('Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back').

Redline is directionally correct and actionable: it reverses the assignment to Customer, expressly preserves Vendor Technology under 14.3 and the Section 13.2 perpetual licence for embedded Vendor IP, so it does not overreach into Vendor's pre-existing IP.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.747 changed-character ratio) is expected here — reversing an ownership/assignment direction and removing the revocable term-limited licence sentence necessarily rewrites the clause; no smaller edit reaches the playbook position.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the fallback (Vendor ownership plus perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence with modify/sublicense rights) as a negotiation landing zone.

Other IP sub-elements (Customer Data ownership in 14.1, Vendor Technology retention in 14.3, no joint ownership in 14.4) are correctly noted as satisfactory rather than re-flagged, so there is no double-counting or over-flagging.
